text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet today is expected to discuss a report between cabinet representatives and farmers, although farmers' leaders indicated they are not satisfied with the outcome of those talks. Half-lane closures are expected on only 24 roads today. @
- Visiting German President Roman Herzog praised Hungary Wednesday for its "exemplary" minority police, while visiting a community of ethnic Germans near Budapest.
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said he hoped that a nationwide agreement on wages and pensions could help reduce inflation to 9 percent by the end of next year.

- Culture and Education Minister Balint Magyar has sent a letter to his Slovak counterpart protesting against measures passed in Slovakia that have a disadvantageous effect on the education of the Hungarian minority. @
- Erno Kiss, director of the Central Crime Fighting Directorate complained that only HUF 49 million of the HUF 680 million set aside last year could be used.
- Hungary's net foreign debt went down by about $2.5 bilion to $12.9 billion at current prices last year, the National Bank announced.

- The government will soon launch an examination project of Hungarian industrial companies in order to assess their readiness for the country's EU membership, said Industry and Trade Minister Szabolcs Fazakas. @
- Queen Elizabeth II yesterday unveiled a statue of Raoul Wallenberg, the Swedish diplomat who saved thousands of Hungarian Jews during World War II.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Endre Juhasz, Hungary's ambassador to the European Commission, said that Commission is expected to give a positive assessment of Hungary, enabling it to join talks on admission, but warned the critical remarks must also be anticipated.
- Danuta Hubner, Poland's state secretary for EuroAtlantic integration matters, is in Budapest to discuss preparations for NATO and EU membership. @
- The National Bank of Hungary will decrease its base rate by 1 percent to 21.5 percent as of March 1.

- Hungary took an important step towards economic stability last year, as the country's internal and external economic equilibrium have improved considerably, according to a joint study by the economic research firm GKI and Postabank.
- Smoke-detection equipment capable of recording vehicle exhaust fumes will begin operating in Budapest from March 1.
- A 29-year-old Chinese woman was found dead in her Budapest apartment yesterday. She was the fifth victim in the past few weeks. @
- Customs guards seized almost 54 kilograms of heroin found in the toolbag of a Turkish truck at the border station of Nagylak.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Another 13 percent in the Richter pharmaceutical company will be offered to foreign and, later, Hungarian investors by late May, the State Privatisation and Holding Co. decided. @

- The German owner of the meat processor Szekszardi Husipari Rt. has breached the privatisation contract by failing to carry out a HUF 400 million capital increase, said State Privatisation and Holding Co. CEO Pal Szabo. The owner is compelled to pay a HUF 100 million fine.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
